differences.title: 1. METADATA MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Hudi uses versioning at the row level, enabling efficient upserts and deletes. It maintains a metadata log of file versions for data manipulation operations.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg manages metadata through atomic commits of file manifests. Each commit represents a consistent snapshot of the table, ensuring ACID properties.

differences.title: 2. PARTITION EVOLUTION
differences.leftDesc: Hudi's partition evolution is more complex, often requiring rewriting data or using specific modes. It's less dynamic for frequent schema or partition changes.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg supports seamless partition evolution without rewriting existing data files. It handles schema and partition evolution gracefully, adapting to changes easily.

differences.title: 3. WRITE OPERATIONS
differences.leftDesc: Hudi offers Copy-on-Write (CoW) for immediate consistency or Merge-on-Read (MoR) for efficient updates and deletes with separate delta logs.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg primarily uses an append-only file model, with MoR being a common pattern. Updates are written to new files, and reads merge them.

differences.title: 4. CONCURRENCY CONTROL
differences.leftDesc: Hudi employs optimistic locking mechanisms, detecting and handling write conflicts based on file versions and last commit times.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg uses optimistic concurrency control, relying on atomic metadata operations and version tracking to ensure consistency during concurrent writes.

differences.title: 5. TABLE SCHEMA EVOLUTION
differences.leftDesc: Hudi can handle schema evolution at the record level within files, offering flexibility for evolving data structures.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg manages schema evolution at the table level, enforcing schema compatibility and providing robust support for adding, dropping, or renaming columns.

differences.title: 6. TIME TRAVEL
differences.leftDesc: Hudi's time travel is based on committed versions of data files, allowing queries against specific commits or past states.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg's time travel is achieved by querying historical snapshots identified by timestamp or snapshot ID, offering precise historical views.

differences.title: 7. ECOSYSTEM INTEGRATION
differences.leftDesc: Hudi has deep integration with Spark and Hadoop ecosystems, optimized for these environments and their tools.
differences.rightDesc: Iceberg offers broader engine support, including Spark, Flink, Trino, and Hive, making it adaptable across various processing frameworks.
